output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) reported dispute tickets doubling and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix bills (CL-01). Investigation (crm-tickets, billing-db, route-log, mdms-export, billing-config) confirmed the surge: ~600/month in Jun-Jul rose to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep (E-07). An initial problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed part of it to a field-staffing shortage reducing manual-read route completion (E-01, E-06), but this was INVALIDATED once E-11 showed that 95.5% (1184 of 1240) of disputed ESTIMATED-read bills actually had valid, on-time AMI reads that were rejected during billing import, not missing reads. The problem was redefined (PD-1@v2): billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-12), wrongly rejects valid high-consumption AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution for 1184 accounts (E-11/E-13/E-14/E-15), confirmed by H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-IMPORT-REJE and H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE. Whether this same rule also inflates the larger ACTUAL-read dispute segment (59% of all disputes) is unconfirmed. The DEFINE gate passed CONDITIONALLY, deferring several questions to open Verification Obligations (VOBs). Given budget and tool-write constraints (no automated bill writes per K-BILLWRITE), the release was scoped only to reviewing the AMI export log (review_ami_export_log:DA-MDMS); the actual BV-17 code fix and rebilling of affected accounts were judged infeasible within the contest window. The final decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: the diagnostic finding about BV-17 and the ESTIMATED-read population is released, while several questions remain open and documented as known limitations rather than blocking the release.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS): build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and fix wrong bills; treated as an unverified claim, not an established fact.

Dispute volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07/F-06); SLA response times remain within target (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d, E-04), so this is not a response-speed problem (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING rejected).
Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) are ESTIMATED-read and 1785 (59%) are ACTUAL-read (E-02).

An earlier theory that field staffing shortfall and route under-completion (E-01, E-06, E-09) drove the ESTIMATED-read disputes was invalidated by E-11: 95.5% (1184/1240) of those bills had valid, timely AMI reads rejected on billing import, not missing reads.

Root cause confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read segment: billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-12) rejects valid high-consumption AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, affecting 1184 accounts, all firmware v4.2 (E-11, E-13, E-14, E-15).

It remains unconfirmed whether BV-17 also inflates computed consumption on ACTUAL-read bills, which could explain the larger 59% ACTUAL-read dispute majority (H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-ACTUAL, VOB-U-BV17-ACTUAL-READ-IMPACT, still OPEN/CRITICAL).

The release scope was limited to review_ami_export_log:DA-MDMS; the structural fix to BV-17 and rebilling of the 1184 affected accounts were judged not feasible within the contest/harness time window and were not executed.
No automated writes to customer bills were made or proposed, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint requiring Billing Operations approval for any bill adjustment.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate for this problem passed as CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some open questions were deliberately deferred and tracked as Verification Obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before proceeding.

Three VOBs remain OPEN and are outside the current release scope: whether BV-17 also inflates ACTUAL-read bills (VOB-U-BV17-ACTUAL-READ-IMPACT, CRITICAL), and two concerns about whether dispute-volume/ticket-share metrics could be gamed by ticket deflection rather than real bill-correctness improvement (VOB-U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI, VOB-U-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDITY, both HIGH).

The actual code patch to BV-17 (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) and the rebilling of the 1184 affected accounts (SR-REBILL-AFFECTED-ESTIMATED-AC) were identified as the real structural remedies but are marked not feasible within this contest/harness time window, so they were not executed.

Because the ACTUAL-read mechanism is unconfirmed, two review actions (review_actual_read_consumption_calculation:DA-BILL and review_billing_rule_change_log:DA-RULES) are withheld from this release pending resolution of VOB-U-BV17-ACTUAL-READ-IMPACT.

The 56 of 1240 (4.5%) ESTIMATED-read disputed bills with NO_READ_RECEIVED status (E-11) are not explained by the BV-17 mechanism and remain an open residual question (U-RESIDUAL-HANDOFF-OR-AMI-GAP) about whether a field handoff or AMI delivery gap is responsible.

Dispute response handling currently meets its SLA (E-04) and any remediation must not be allowed to regress that performance; this is flagged as a constraint to preserve, not something fixed by this release.

Volume and ticket-share metrics could in principle be improved by ticket deflection or auto-closure (e.g., an automated answering agent) without the underlying bill-correctness problem actually improving; this risk is only partially mitigated by cross-checking against the rejection-rate metric, not fully resolved.
